title: Powerdevil does not respect lid-switch inhibitor created with systemd-inhibit
line: Closing the lid no longer suspends the laptop while a program holds a handle-lid-switch inhibitor, such as systemd-inhibit; it suspends once that inhibitor is released.
explanation: PowerDevil holds its own logind handle-lid-switch inhibitor so that it, not logind, reacts to the lid. It then ran the configured lid action unconditionally, so a handle-lid-switch inhibitor taken by another program (systemd-inhibit, a presentation tool) was ignored, while without PowerDevil logind would have respected it. The lid action (on lid close, after an unwanted wakeup and after an external display is unplugged) now first asks logind for block inhibitors on handle-lid-switch held by other processes; if there is one it skips the action and checks again every 5 seconds while the lid stays closed, running it once the inhibitor is gone. Opening the lid stops the checks.

commits.message:
daemon: Respect lid switch inhibitors from other applications

PowerDevil took over lid handling from logind and then ran the lid action
even when another program held a handle-lid-switch inhibitor. Check for
such inhibitors on lid close and wait until they are released instead.

BUG: 485623

media.caption: Master: with systemd-inhibit --what=handle-lid-switch held, closing the lid still suspends at once and again after the wakeup check.
Fix: no suspend while the inhibitor is held; suspend 2 s after it is released with the lid still closed. Without an inhibitor the lid suspends as before.
